title: Tinjau EvidenceGraphView
description: Claim, provenance and relationship structure behind one risk assessment. Produced by apps/server/src/evidence/{normalize,cluster,graph}.ts. Every field here is DERIVED from source text or from deterministic rules — none of it is a model's free-form opinion, and none of it may be edited by a consumer. CURRENT AS OF 2026-08-21: instantiated by the `.evidenceGraph` field of scenario-rumor-watch.json and scenario-confirmed-protect.json, assembled in frontend-handoff/tools/generate.ts from the production modules and checked against this file by frontend-handoff/tools/validate.mjs. `rejectedProposals` is empty in both, and that is the honest value rather than a stub: the four scenarios' clusters were frozen by hand in T0.2, so no model proposal existed to reject.

eventKey.description: Stable identity for the underlying event. Claims about one event share it.

label.description: Human-readable event name. Never used in any decision.

evidenceWindowSeconds.description: How far back evidence may be published and still count. Frozen in promotionConfig.ts.

independentOriginCount.description: Distinct non-rumour origins after syndications are collapsed.

usableOriginCount.description: Origins that may actually corroborate: independentOriginCount minus those disqualified by self-revision. THIS is the number the promotion rules count, not independentOriginCount. A UI showing the larger number beside a WATCH would make the decision look arbitrary.

revisedOriginKeys.description: Origins that stated more than one figure for this event and therefore cannot corroborate.

rejectedProposals.description: Cluster proposals the deterministic rules refused. Present so a model's failure is visible rather than silent; usually empty.

sourceClass.description: RUMOR can never authorise an action, whatever the market shows.

dataMode.description: SIMULATED means fabricated for testing. A consumer MUST render it distinctly — it is not evidence of anything real.

assertionLevel.description: How strongly the SOURCE asserted the claim, derived from its own language. Never compare these with </> to gate anything; detection may only ever weaken a claim, never strengthen it.

sourceUrl.description: null is CORRECT for a SIMULATED claim and a defect for anything else. A simulated claim carrying a resolvable URL is the most dangerous shape in this system — it looks checkable and is not — and is flagged as a violation.

publishedAtPrecision.description: A DAY-precision timestamp must not be rendered as though it were exact to the second.

sourceContentSha256.description: sha256 of the exact source bytes. Mandatory for OFFICIAL claims; that is what lets a third party verify the document rather than trust Tinjau.

claimTextOrPointer.description: Verbatim span or a pointer to one. NEVER a paraphrase — paraphrasing is how speculation becomes fact.

describesCompletedEvent.description: DERIVED from the source's own language, never supplied. False for anything framed as talks, plans, or possibilities. A claim about talks is evidence that talks are happening, not that a deal exists.

speculationMarkers.description: Exactly which hedging phrases matched, so the call can be checked rather than trusted.

publisherDisclaimedVerification.description: True when the publisher itself said it could not confirm the claim.

officialConfirmation.description: Whether an official document later confirmed this claim. This is NOT the same as describesCompletedEvent, which is about what this source asserted at the time. A hedged report that a filing later confirms is the normal shape of breaking financial news.

materiality.description: Separate axis from provenance. A routine Section 16 Form 4 is an impeccably-sourced OFFICIAL filing that reports no corporate action; promoting on it would raise LP fees for nothing. UNKNOWN fails closed.

promotable.description: DERIVED from provenanceViolations being empty, never supplied. A non-promotable claim is kept and displayed, not discarded — that record is what makes a WATCH explainable.

outcome.description: UNSUPPORTED_ASSET means the token is known but has no verified pool — e.g. NVDAx, the unwrapped sibling of wNVDAx. It is registered deliberately so a claim about it refuses loudly rather than reading as a coverage gap.

asset.description: Non-null only when outcome is RESOLVED.

mayAuthorizeAction.description: DERIVED. True for exactly one outcome, RESOLVED. Ambiguity is a refusal, not a tie-break.

derivedOriginKey.description: Canonical origin this claim's reporting traces back to, derived from attribution phrases in the text and byline.

isSyndication.description: True when the claim attributes its reporting to a different outlet. Several syndications of one origin count as ONE source — that invariant is what stops four headlines from looking like four independent confirmations.

evidence.description: The matched attribution phrase, so the derivation is checkable rather than magic.

relaysUnnamedReport.description: True for a claim that admits it is relaying a report but never says whose — e.g. a headline ending '- report'. It cannot be merged into an origin and must not be counted as one, since independence is precisely what it disclaimed.

disagreesWithDeclared.description: True when the derivation and the fixture's hand label disagree. Surfaced, never auto-resolved — either could be wrong, and which is right is a question for a human.

revised.description: True when one source line stated more than one figure for this event. Such a line may support a WATCH but cannot count toward independent corroboration: it has not established the fact, only that the number is still moving.

fromFuture.description: A claim dated after the assessment instant. A data defect, surfaced rather than silently accepted.

confidenceFactor.description: Every confidence change carries one of these. §0.9 requires a machine-readable explanation for why confidence changed — a bare number would be unauditable.

reason.description: UNKNOWN_CLAIM_ID means a proposal named a claim that does not exist — a hallucination, rejected rather than repaired. DUPLICATE_CLAIM_ASSIGNMENT would have let one claim count twice toward independence, which is the one arithmetic that must not be inflatable.
